findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition silently replaces the original API
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading, so the new three-argument self.downsize at line 149 replaces the four-argument self.downsize defined at line 145. Existing callers that pass separate max_width and max_height (optionally with opts) will now raise ArgumentError instead of resizing, while the first definition becomes dead code. Remove the old definition and update all callers, or implement a single signature that handles both dimension forms.

findings.title: Client upload limit is hardcoded and ignores site and file-type settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments could have different configured limits. Replacing it with a constant 10 MB rejects valid uploads on sites configured above 10 MB and accepts attachments or images that the server will later reject on sites configured below 10 MB. The same hardcoded value at line 246 also makes the 413 error message report 10 MB regardless of the actual configured limit.

findings.title: Remote-image download cap no longer respects max_image_size_kb
findings.body: FileHelper.download is now always limited to 10 megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. Sites allowing images larger than 10 MB will fail to fetch otherwise valid remote images, while sites with a smaller limit will download and process needlessly large files before downsizing. The pre-downsize fetch cap should be derived consistently with the client limit and the configured settings.

findings.title: Percentage downsizing is passed to gifsicle as an invalid WxH dimension
findings.body: The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the dimension string "80%", but for animated GIFs downsize_instructions_animated forwards that string to resize_instructions_animated, producing `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle expects a WxH size for --resize-fit (percentage scaling is done with --scale), so the command fails, animated GIFs are not downsized, and the controller retries the failing command five times before the oversized upload is rejected.

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored while converting the upload in place
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize returns false when conversion or optimization fails, but this loop ignores the result and repeats the operation up to five times on the same tempfile.path used as both source and destination. A failing or partially successful conversion therefore wastes expensive ImageMagick/ImageOptim runs and can leave the only copy of the upload truncated or converted before Upload.create_for consumes it. Convert to a separate temporary output, check the result, and only replace the original after a successful downsize (breaking out of the loop on failure).

findings.title: No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior
findings.body: The PR adds the downsize loop, changes OptimizedImage.downsize's public signature, and changes client/server size limits, but adds no specs. There is no coverage that an oversized image is reduced below max_image_size_kb, that an image still oversized after five attempts is rejected cleanly, that animated GIFs work, or that existing width/height downsize callers still function, so regressions such as the duplicate downsize definition would not be caught.
